generator: Built-in image_gen tool (codex-imagegen skill when the session has no image tool)
purpose: Company HQ command-deck banner: the flagship's operations deck with Castle and the watch on duty. Stations are fixed so hotspots can be mapped onto them; see the hq-command-deck.md story.

master.runtimeCrop: Centre band, 5:1. The top and bottom 20% of the master may be cut, so nothing that matters may sit there.
master.reference: Pass art-source/portraits/castle/castle-master.png as a reference image if the tool accepts one, so Castle on deck matches her dialogue portrait.

prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: wide 3:1 in-universe establishing illustration for Starsector Marines, a grounded mercenary ground-operations game; it becomes a banner across the top of the company's headquarters screen. Style: detailed late-1990s/early-2000s science-fiction strategy-game illustration, matte-painted cinematic industrial realism, visible restrained brush texture, the same painted family as the game's character portraits. Tactile worn metal, scuffed deck plate, cable runs, patched paint. Restrained olive, charcoal, umber and cream palette; warm amber work lights and console glow against a dim ceiling, soft cool fill from a long viewport. Scene: the operations deck of a converted ex-freighter that a mercenary marine company lives aboard. Not a gleaming warship bridge: low ceiling, exposed ribs and conduit, hand-labelled panels with no legible text, coffee mugs and clipped paper on a corkboard. Camera: eye level, slightly elevated, looking across the deck; a long viewport along the back wall shows a dark starfield and the edge of a dusty planet. Composition, left to right, each station clearly separated with deck space between them so they read as distinct places: (1) LEFT, a comms bank: two comms officers seated at chunky console stations with headsets, one turned mid-sentence to the other, banks of small amber screens and patch cables; (2) CENTRE-LEFT, a large backlit chart table lit from below with a warm paper-like glow, a commander standing over it seen from behind and slightly to one side, face not visible, broad-shouldered in a worn officer's field coat, both hands planted on the table edge; (3) CENTRE-RIGHT, Castle standing at the far side of the chart table facing the commander and the viewer: a woman in her early fifties, warm pale olive skin, dark brown hair with silver at the temples tied in a short practical bun, worn charcoal-olive high-collared duty jacket, small earpiece with a short boom microphone, holding a battered data slate, restrained knowing half-smile, attentive and calm; (4) RIGHT, a logistics and ledger station: a quartermaster type leaning on a standing desk with stacked manifests and a small screen of columns, a crate of supplies at his feet; (5) FAR RIGHT, an open bulkhead hatch with a ladder down and a crew roster board beside it covered in name tags. Keep every person, face, hand and console inside the middle 60% of the frame height; the top 20% is plain ceiling and lights, the bottom 20% is plain deck. Leave the lower-right third of the middle band visually quiet (dark deck and console shadow) because interface text will sit there. Five to six figures in total, natural proportions, nobody looking at the camera except Castle's slight glance. Constraints: no text, lettering, numbers, logos, insignia, HUD elements, frames or watermark. No holograms, no blue neon, no glass touchscreens floating in air, no weapons drawn, no battle, no gore, no giant mechs, no huge spaceships in the viewport. Original characters only, no resemblance to actors or existing game characters. Opaque, edge-to-edge painting.

prompts.use: Optional second state, shown while an obligation is overdue. Generate only after the main plate is approved.
prompts.prompt: Edit the supplied command-deck illustration. Keep the composition, every figure, every station and every pose exactly where they are. Change only the lighting and small cues: the warm work lights dim, a pulsing red-amber alert lamp washes the ceiling and back wall, console screens shift to urgent amber, the comms officers lean in toward their screens and one presses her earpiece, Castle looks down at her data slate with a focused expression. No text, numbers, logos, HUD or holograms. Same painted style and palette.
